purpose: REGF3 version of grid B: the same network, operating point and events, with the REGF3 unit (dVOC) in the slot; the selection grid for the held-out device.

case.name: grid_B3
case.description: Kundur two-area re-arranged: device in GENROU 3's slot; one of the three 7-8 tie circuits (Line_6) out of service; a new 200 MW load PQ_3 at the device's HV bus 9; 150 MW load PQ_2 at bus 10; loads moved from bus 8 to bus 7; device at 720 MW (above any training dispatch) with a 1.02 pu voltage schedule; device REGF3

device_under_test.params_note: ANDES inputs. The six REGF1 parameters drawn the way REGF1's and REGF2's were (ANDES defaults scaled by numpy default_rng(seed).uniform(0.7, 1.3, 6) in the order wdrp, Qdrp, Tpm, KPplim, KIplim, Tr; wdrp and Qdrp times Sb/Sn), with seed 2, so the three units share no numbers; KPv = 6 as for the other two. REGF3 (dVOC) has no parameters of its own: its dVOC gain Kdvoc is a constant ANDES computes from wdrp and Qdrp (about 1.6e-10 here), and Qdrp enters only through it. The same device sits in grids A3, B3 and M3.

design_notes: Grid B with REGF3 instead of REGF1 (Nov 15), so the held-out device is tested on the grids the two training devices were tuned on and only the device differs. Grid M's dispatch and schedule were chosen for REGF1's damping; they have not been re-checked for REGF3.

Under REGF3 the staged voltage-reference steps barely move the unit: ANDES's dVOC gain Kdvoc is about 1e-10, so Vset enters its equations almost not at all, and in steady state the unit holds Q (no Q-V droop). The steps are kept so the events match grids B and B2 exactly.

The device's loading decides whether a voltage-loop error is visible at all. At 550 MW a 30% error in the voltage-loop gain KPv cost 0.02 to 0.06 on a line trip, at 700 MW 0.16 to 0.22, and at grid A's op1 it saturates. 720 MW keeps that error visible without saturating and sits just above the training dispatch.
